findings.title: Validator has DB write side-effect and non-atomic counter
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at and calls save, and it is called from EmailValidator.validate_each on every User validation where email changed. That means a read/validation path writes to the database, updates stats even for validations that ultimately fail or are just probed, and does read-modify-write via match_count += 1 plus save which loses increments under concurrent signups and can fail validation silently.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, the lookup is BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with no downcasing/normalization, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. Since email addresses are case-insensitive, an attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or Bad@Spammers.org and BlockedEmail.should_block? will return false, defeating the block.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist regex allows suffix bypass
findings.body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end-anchor after escaping only dots. A whitelist entry like allowed.com therefore matches user@allowed.com.evil.com, so an attacker can pass the whitelist (or dodge/match the blacklist incorrectly) by appending a suffix domain, defeating the domain restriction.
